title: Interfaces That Keep Thinking
content:
## Interfaces That Keep Thinking

A useful tool is not a vending machine for output. It is a surface that keeps the next decision visible. When the surface is good, the writer can see where the argument is thin, where a phrase is doing too much work, and where a note deserves to live beside the paragraph instead of below it.

> the best tools do not finish your thought; they keep your thought inspectable.

That is the bar I want for tiny personal software: it should hold context, expose friction, and refuse silent failure.

## Anchors Before Notes

Margin notes only work when the anchor is stable. If the note points at text that later disappears, the note becomes decoration with no contract. A note generator should therefore do three things before it celebrates: find a unique anchor, show the section it belongs to, and warn when a phrase is too vague.

A repeatable checkpoint phrase belongs here so the tool can prove it knows when a short anchor is ambiguous.

The writer should ask for better anchors before it saves broken annotations. That small refusal is useful because it protects the published reading experience.

## Suggestion Is Not Authorship

Suggestions are best when they behave like a careful editor. They should point at sentences that already carry tension: a claim, a reversal, a question, or a definition. They should not invent footnotes for every paragraph. Scarcity makes each side note feel intentional.

The same repeatable checkpoint phrase appears here, which means a lazy note anchored to only that phrase should be rejected as ambiguous.

A good suggestion is a door handle. It tells the writer: "this is where a reader may want a little more context."

## The Small Contract

The contract is simple:

1. the editor keeps the draft fast.
2. the preview shows what readers will actually see.
3. the margin-note tool validates anchors before export.
4. the exported JSON renders without a cleanup pass.

If that loop holds, publishing feels less like formatting and more like thinking in public.

```text
draft -> preview -> anchored note -> JSON -> rendered essay
```

The tool does not need to be clever everywhere. It just needs to be stubborn at the places where a broken note would become invisible later.
